posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.content_md:
I ventured into split beam holography this weekend.

My set up is a little conventional and will do my best to discribe it.

My Melles Griot laser has two 200mw beams exiting the laser slightly off axis to each other.

I am using one as my reference and the object beam is split by a 50/50 beam splitter which illuminate both sides of the object. 

The object was set about 2 inches away from the plate

I used DCG

Processed for BB (which I know limits depth but shouldn't be this much)

The path length is not exact but I was told that with the long coherrence lenght leser that exactness is not an issue.

I illuminated the object as hight I as could go. I was not able to tell my ratio (ob/ref) because a lot of light was getting through my DCG, so I went for max. I never seen noise before so I don't know if this is what I am experencing.

The photo which is not a good one but shows that the image is blurry not sharp at all.

Can you please tell me some of the possible causes?

If you need more info, let me know.

Thanks in advance.

Tony

posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.content_md:
I talked to Danny on the phone and he suggested that I try an LED. This cleared it up nicely.

So is there any thing I can do to make a broadband DCG with depth?

Thanks

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
If you look at the equations the two parameters are mutually exclusive. There are other ideas. Exposing two frequencies or black and white holography for instance. 

Have some of the depth in front of the film plane helps as well.

posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.content_md: Hey Colin, at the risk of sounding completing dumb can you elaborate a bit more.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: I think Colin's suggesting making a narrow band, 2-color reflection hologram, or use a dispersion compensation grating. For laser illumination when used as an H1, it shouldn't matter.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
Sorry, I was in a hurry and had my 2 year old tugging at me. 

> So is this due to the fact that it is a white broadband image and my light source (point source) is focusing different colors at different depths?

This is exactly the problem. Near the plate the problem is small but the farther you go back of front the dispersion increases.
